record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: Among vacuum Einstein spacetimes with compact spatial manifold T^3, is the flat product spacetime T^3 × R the only spacetime that is both future complete and past complete?

evidence.quote: It is conjectured, and partially proved, that the manifold T3 × R with the flat metric is the only future and past complete Einsteinian spacetime;

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider smooth 4-dimensional Lorentzian manifolds $(M, g)$ that satisfy the vacuum Einstein equations $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = 0$ and admit a Cauchy hypersurface diffeomorphic to the 3-torus $T^3 = S^1 \times S^1 \times S^1$. Call such a spacetime future complete (respectively past complete) if every future-inextendible (respectively past-inextendible) timelike geodesic has infinite affine length. The flat product spacetime $(T^3 \times \mathbb{R}, h_{\mathrm{flat}} \oplus (-dt^2))$, where $h_{\mathrm{flat}}$ is a flat Riemannian metric on $T^3$, is both future and past complete.

Question: Is the flat product spacetime $T^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ (up to isometry) the only globally hyperbolic vacuum spacetime with Cauchy surface $T^3$ that is simultaneously future complete and past complete?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is the well-known conjecture (often attributed to Fischer–Moncrief and Anderson) that the flat metric on $T^3 \times \mathbb{R}$ is the unique geodesically complete vacuum spacetime with $T^3$ Cauchy surface. Only partial results are known: future completeness for small perturbations near the flat solution has been established, and rigidity results restrict possible behaviors, but no full proof of uniqueness has appeared. The conjecture remains open.

status_evidence.title: Future Complete Vacuum Spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Results on future-complete vacuum spacetimes with compact spatial topology, including perturbative results around the flat T^3 model.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (perturbative) results toward the conjecture are available.

status_evidence.title: A large data result for vacuum Einstein's equations
status_evidence.snippet: Global existence results for spatially compact vacuum spacetimes in expanding direction.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to address completeness for vacuum Einstein equations with compact spatial slices, indicating the full uniqueness statement is not yet resolved.
